analysis: Examined base-side test units for SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift lines 3039-4237 (whole-root maintainer tests, donation gate, outcomes, windowed sidecar tests). The only change in this file (head 3140-3240) adds tests asserting that SSDWholeRootMaintainer re-verifies DBK3 header ownership when a file changes (ctime-based) even if size/mtime are restored, and that a replaced malformed lookalike becomes owned on the next pass. This implies production code now caches header verdicts keyed on file identity/size/mtime/ctime; the tests assert fail-safe behavior (changed file loses ownership proof and is not deleted). Test-only change; no production source supplied, so the actual verdict-cache implementation (cache key fields, inode reuse, symlink/no-follow handling per SSDNoFollowIO, bounded cache size) is outside this evidence. Relevant threat T-041 (at-rest DBK3 cleanup, TTL/LRU eviction, ownership proof before unlink). No regression identified from tests alone. Integration should verify the maintainer's verdict cache in Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD (likely SSDWholeRootMaintainer / SSDBlockStore) keys on dev+inode+size+mtime+ctime, never treats a stale positive verdict as ownership for a replaced non-DBK3 file (risk: deleting operator files in an operator-selected root), and bounds memory growth.
